subject: Post-demo engine scouting: shortlist + commercial/ops tradeoffs
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@catalyst-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo engine scouting: shortlist + commercial/ops tradeoffs

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and very helpful context on the high-throughput question and the mixed prompt lengths you run (short routing prompts + occasional long summaries). Below is a concise post-demo recap and our recommended next steps.

Quick recap
- Goal: reduce per-query unit costs while preserving summary quality for Finance reports and keeping p95 latency under 250ms for typical short prompts.
- Key constraints you reiterated: (1) strict 3-month pilot budget, (2) production traces available for benchmark replay, (3) on-prem data retention for audit logs.

Recommended 3-engine shortlist (balanced by cost / latency / quality)
1) Compact-v2 (q4) — low cost, smallest token cost, very good for short prompts; expected median latency ~70–120ms on our Dedicated pool; quality slightly below the 13B FP models on abstractive summarization but acceptable with prompt engineering.
2) Aurora-13B (fp16) — quality leader in the shortlist; higher per-token cost, median latency ~140–200ms; best pick if highest summary fidelity is the priority.
3) EdgeLite-7B (int8) — best low-latency fallback for synchronous UIs; lowest tail latency at modest cost, but needs careful tuning for long-form summaries.

Tradeoffs (short)
- Cost vs quality: Compact-v2 (q4) is cost-efficient but requires prompt calibration and a small set of post-processing checks. Aurora-13B gives the cleanest output out-of-the-box at a material cost premium.
- Latency: EdgeLite-7B is the fastest for p95; Compact-v2 is a good middle ground with batching.
- Regression risk: rolling a quantized model (q4) into production can surface occasional quality regressions on rare prompt patterns (we flag these with targeted evals).

Attachments included:
- catalyst_benchmarks_20280615.csv (initial synthetic replay metrics)
- prompt_sets_v1.zip (your supplied traces anonymized + our canonical prompts)
- ma_planned.csv (draft mutual action plan template)

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Permission to run a 48-hour replay benchmark against your traces starting Tue 2028-06-20 (we'll push results to the Drive link).
2) Agree target quality acceptance criteria (e.g., >=85% pass rate on the human eval rubric we reviewed).
3) Pilot canary plan: start with 5–10% traffic on Compact-v2, Aurora-13B as fallback for failed thresholds; after 72-hour stability, increase to 50%.

If that aligns, I'll schedule the benchmark and loop in engineering for the pilot kickoff.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Rafael — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we greenlight the replay: 
1) Can you share expected per-token cost ranges (ballpark) for the three engines when using our estimated 20M tokens/month footprint?
2) Will the Compact-v2 q4 candidate preserve named-entity fidelity for our financial entities? We've seen quantized runs that copy hallucinated ticker names when prompts are noisy.
3) For the pilot, we want the benchmark to run on production traces — is there an easy path to securely share a filtered trace (PII removed) and have Redwood run it in a locked VPC?

If those answers look fine we can confirm Tue 6/20 start. Attaching an internal note with the budget window.

— Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Product, Catalyst Analytics
sara@catalyst-analytics.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara@catalyst-analytics.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo engine scouting: shortlist + commercial/ops tradeoffs

Rafael — short answers for Sara (so we can move fast):
- Per-token cost (ballpark, hosted pricing equivalents):
  • Compact-v2 (q4): ~$0.0008–0.0012 per token (depends on batching & caching).
  • Aurora-13B (fp16): ~$0.0020–0.0035 per token.
  • EdgeLite-7B (int8): ~$0.0010–0.0016 per token.
- Named-entity fidelity: quantized Compact-v2 may need a small targeted prompt set and a 1–2% guardrail filter (post-check) for ticker/entity copy issues. We'll include that in the prompt pack.
- VPC replay: yes — we can accept a filtered trace via a secure S3 share or a locked Drive folder and run the replay in a dedicated sandbox; we will not persist the trace outside the sandbox.

I've uploaded the initial benchmark CSV to the Drive folder and attached prompt_sets_v1.zip + ma_planned.csv to this thread.

—Kimberly

Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo engine scouting: shortlist + commercial/ops tradeoffs

Thanks Sara / Kim — appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming scope and next steps so the Catalyst team has an explicit playbook. 

Confirmed scope
- Replay start: Tue 2028-06-20 09:00 PT (48 hours). Redwood runs in a dedicated sandbox (locked S3 / ephemeral infra).
- Engines we'll bench: Compact-v2 (q4), Aurora-13B (fp16), EdgeLite-7B (int8).
- Metrics we'll report: tokenized cost estimate, median + p95 latency, top-line human-eval pass % on the supplied rubric, and a short set of failure examples for any regression concerns.

Canary pilot proposal (high level)
- Week 0: 48h replay and calibration. Output: tuned prompt set + baseline metrics.
- Week 1 (canary): 5–10% production traffic to Compact-v2 behind Redwood Optimize checks (regression guardrails + sampling). Aurora-13B will be available as a fallback for flagged requests.
- Escalation policy: if human-eval pass drops under the agreed threshold (we set 85% unless you counter), we hold traffic and rollback to Aurora fallback.

Operational notes / risk mitigations
- Quality regression monitoring: We'll wire the Redwood Optimize regression alerting to your Slack channel and create an eval set for nightly regression runs.
- KV/prefix caching: for your short routing prompts we expect a 20–35% effective token reduction with prefix caching enabled — that will materially improve cost on Compact-v2.
- Audit & retention: sandbox logs + audit bundle will be delivered to your secure bucket; we will not retain raw trace after run completion unless you opt-in.

Commercial ask
- Pilot: $8k flat for the 2-week pilot (includes dedicated sandbox, replay, 1 tuning iteration, and alerting set-up). If acceptable, we'll issue a short pilot SOW via DocuSign and schedule a kickoff.

Please confirm: (A) pilot budget ok, (B) you confirm the quality threshold (85% vs 90%), (C) agree to start 6/20. Once confirmed Kimberly will kick off the sandbox provisioning.

Thanks — Rafael
